DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Cancer.

The clinical picture of a large ovarian mass, significant ascites, and shortness of breath in a 40-year-old woman is highly suggestive of advanced ovarian malignancy, despite the normal CA-125. The ultrasound confirms the presence of the mass and fluid accumulation, which explains your respiratory symptoms due to pressure on the diaphragm. We need to proceed with a referral for surgical evaluation and staging.
